claims.text: An IF statement selects between paths: IF <condition> THEN ... ELSE ... ENDIF, with nested IF statements placing a further selection inside a branch to test a second condition after the first.

claims.text: Each side of AND or OR is a complete comparison, so IF X = "a" OR X = "b" is written in full, and the one-sided form IF X = "a" OR "b" is not a condition at all.

claims.text: A FOR loop suits a repetition whose count is known before the loop starts, whereas WHILE and REPEAT loops suit repetitions that end on a condition, because the count cannot be said in advance.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A WHILE loop tests its condition before the body runs, so the body may run zero times, whereas a REPEAT loop runs the body once before its first test, so the body runs at least once.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Justifying a loop is answering the two questions: can the number of iterations be said before the loop starts - if not, no FOR - and must the body run at least once - if so, REPEAT fits; if the body may need to run zero times, WHILE fits.

claims.text: A loop must contain a statement that moves its condition towards its end, because a WHILE whose condition nothing inside changes runs forever.
